2. The appellant by filing the Writ petition challenged legality of the order dated August 22, 1978 passed by respondent No.1 dismissing him from service on the ground of misconduct. His case in short is that he joined the service of the then Pakistan Council of Scientific and Industrial Research Laboratories, Karachi in the year 1962 as a Junior Technician and was promoted to the post of Technician on September 10, 1965 and thereafter he was promoted to the post of Senior Technician on September 10, 1968. After liberation of Bangladesh the appellant returned from Pakistan and reported to the relevant Ministry for duty; and the Ministry after accepting his joining report sent him to the Bangladesh Council of Scientific and Industrial Research Laboratories, Dacca, hereinafter referred to as "the Council", for duty. The Council absorbed the appellant in the Administration Branch and subsequently in 1974 the appellant was transferred to the technical side where he was given some additional job with additional remuneration. When the appellant was serving in such positron, he was served with notice dated October 12, 1976 alleging inter alia, that he had visited the office of the Superintendent, Establishment Branch-1 of the Council on June 24, 1976 and misbehaved with the Superintendent, The petitioner was asked to show cause within ten days from the receipt of the notice as to why disciplinary action should not be taken against him. He submitted his explanation on October 21, 1976 denying the allegations. After about 7 months the petitioners received notice dated May 4, 1977 by which he was charged sheeted on the ground of misbehavior as his explanation was found unsatisfactory. The appellant submitted his explanation to the charge,within time. No action was taken till August 22, 1977 when the appellant was served with the impugned order of dismissal. The appellant was surprised to receive the said order as the show because notice in question had proposed only minor penalties and the Enquiry Committee recommended his reinstatement. The appellant served demand justice notice through his lawyer. In reply to the same he was informed that the order of dismissal had been passed in connection with the second proceeding and not in connection with the first proceeding. With regard to the other case, the appellant asserted that certain allegations of misconduct were brought against him by the office Memorandum dated March 8, 1977 to which he submitted his written explanation on March 23, 1977 but no enquiry committee was formed to the knowledge of the appellant nor he was required by any official notice to appear before any enquiry committee nor was any charge sheet ever framed against him. The appellant submitted that the dismissal order without any notice served upon him as to the proposed order of dismissal even in connection with the second proceeding was illegal.

Provided that neither the Chairman nor a member shall hold office for more that two consecutive terms, except in a case where the Government is satisfied that the Services of the Chairman or, as the case may be, the Member is required in the interest of the efficient functioning of the Council. Clause 15(B)gives power to the Government to terminate the appointment of the Chairman or any other member without assigning any reason, Clause 16 provides that the Secretary of the council shill be a full time officer and a full time Financial Adviser of the Council who shall be appointed by the Government in consultation with the Chairman. Clause 18 provides for appointment of Officers etc. It provides that the Council may, subject to such general or special order as the Government may issue from time to time, appoint such officers, consultants, advise I and employees as it considers necessary for the efficient performance of its functions on such terms and conditions as may be prescribed in the Bye-Laws of the Council. The clause also provides that the appointment of officers of and above the rank of Senior Research Officers shall be subject to the approval of the Government. 

 (2) All money in the fund of the Council shall be deposited in such bank or banks as may from time to time be approved by the Governing Body, and no money shall be withdrawn from any such bank except on a cheque signed and counter signed by officers authorized in this behalf by the Governing Body. In the absence of the officers so authorized the Chairman shall authorized any officers to officers as the case may be, to sign and Countersign a cheque. Clause 19 provides that all assets of the Pakistan Council of Scientific and Industrial Resources in Bangladesh stood transferred to and vested in the Council. While taking up the assets, the resolution also provides for vesting all debts and liabilities in Bangladesh stands before the publication of the resolution unless the Government otherwise directs, which would be deemed to be debts and liabilities of the Council. 

 18. Now, let us examine whether the High Court Division was correct in holding that the broad principle of natural justice was followed in dismissing the appellant from his service. From the judge it appears that the learned Judgment without proper examination of the question as to whether the order of dismissal was passed in accordance with the provisions of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1976, practically assumed that the principle of natural justice had been followed in the case. In the affidavit in opposition filled before the High Court Division. It has been admitted by the respondents that the Council applied the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeals) Rules, 1976 in the case of its employees at the relevant time. It was specifically contended by the appellant in the Writ Petition that the dismissal order was made, as shown by the respondents, in connection with the second proceeding and not in connection with the first proceeding, and that in second preceding no enquiry was held. Mr. Nabi referred to the different annexures annexed to the Writ Petition and also the affidavit in opposition to show that the respondents failed to produce any materials whatsoever in support of, the respondents case that dismissal order was made after holding due enquiry and in accordance with Rules. 

 19. Mr. S.R. Pal, the learned Counsel, appearing for the respondents also failed to produce any paper before the Court in support of the plea that the dismissal order was made after due enquiry in accordance with the Rules. In our opinion, the learned Judge of the High Court Division were not correct in holding that in the case of the appellant the principle of natural justice was followed, because the finding is not warranted by the materials produced by the respondents. 

 20. From the materials on record it appears that two proceedings were drawn up against the appellant, one on March 15, 1977 on the allegation of misconduct for misbehaving with the Director on February 24,1977 and the appellant was suspended. The other proceeding was drawn up on May 4, 1977 on the allegation of misbehavior with the Superintendent on June 26, 1976. The petitioner submitted his explanation in both the cases. The former called for a major punishment but the latter called for a minor punishment. Annexure E is a letter September 1, 1977 written by the Director of the Council to the lawyer of the appellant. The letter purports to rectify the mistake committed in issuing the letter of dismissal but as a matter of fact no correction was actually made. We have no doubt that in a rather perfunctory manner the. Council dismissed its employee. As per Annexure 'E' read with Annexure 'C' dated August 27, 1977 the appellant was dismissed in connection with the charge-sheet dated May 4, 1977 and the offence for which the charge was framed called for a minor punishment and not a major punishment of dismissal. Therefore, the dismissal of the appellant from his service by Annexure 'C' dated August 22, 1977 cannot be sustained in law and the appellant is entitled to get a declaration that the order of dismissal from his service was without any lawful authority and as such of no legal effect.
